name: basement-membrane-v1
title: From collagen IV turnover to multiscale epithelial morphogenesis (BM v1 → lumenoid)
description:
This investigation is the clean-room Vivarium build of the AICS-Lumenoids
"Basement membrane — v1 model specification" (Roam graph, exported 2026-09-30;
the source spec and diagram are in `workspace/references/`). Every model
parameter is transcribed from the spec's parameter sheet and labelled as such.
The authors' LAMMPS input scripts are now public
(github.com/Billie1717/BasementMembraneTurnoverSims, Zenodo
10.5281/zenodo.20719515, commit `ab4c004`); this build remains a transcription
from the spec rather than a port of those scripts, and they are the ground
truth to cross-check its parameters against (not yet done — decision below).

**Engines.** The workspace imports two already-wrapped simulators —
`viva-lammps` (the `LAMMPSProcess` bridge) and `viva-smoldyn` — and builds the
collagen IV network on top of the real LAMMPS engine. LAMMPS runs stages 1–2
(rigid rods, junction flexibility); Smoldyn is held for stage 3 (flexible
fibers + surface binders) per spec decision #2.

**Staged build.**
  - Stage 1 — reproduce the paper; separate elastic from viscous. Stretch,
    hold, then switch the crosslink chemistry on. Reports an elastic modulus
    and a stress-relaxation time.  ← this investigation's first study.
  - Stage 2 — growing substrate (flat): impose equibiaxial strain rate ε̇,
    read off σ(ε̇); an effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ and the rate at which the
    response turns elastic.
  - Stage 3 — add the cell–BM linker (surface-attached springs, constant
    off-rate). Smoldyn's surface binders land here.
  - Stage 4 — curvature (only if stages 2–3 depend on R beyond ε̇ = Ṙ/R).

**Coupling route.** Offline first: tabulate the BM's modulus
and remodelling time against growth rate and hand them to the vertex model.
Then direct: vertex-mesh surface velocities drive the BM substrate, BM stress
feeds back, exchanged every N vertex steps.

**Visualization (reviewer round 1, 2026-10-07).** Each study's Simularium
trajectory now embeds its diagnostic plots directly (stress-vs-strain, the
stress/strain time series, crosslinks) and draws the periodic simulation box
as a per-frame outline that deforms with the imposed strain. The stretch
movies are made coherent (each bead at its nearest periodic image of the
network centroid), so boundary crossings no longer teleport across timepoints.
See `feedback/` for the imported reviewer file.

**From membrane reproduction to multiscale morphogenesis.** With Barrientos et al.
("Basement membrane turnover controls cell shape", Cell 2026, 189:5611–5624) now
published, this investigation has grown from producing the two numbers a vertex
model needs into a staged reproduction-and-extension study. The plan is to first
reproduce the published tissue and collagen-network results quantitatively, then
replace homogeneous tissue mechanics with spatial 2D and 3D epithelial models
coupled both ways to the membrane, and finally add an explicit actomyosin cortex
and a closed lumenoid geometry. Reproductions, verification, and new predictions
are reported separately.

**Coupling hierarchy.** The epithelium is modelled at increasing spatial detail:
a 2D planar sheet (with a membrane traction/area law and height from a prism
relation), a height-resolving 2D cross-section, a 3D monolayer with apical, basal
and lateral surfaces and volume constraints, and a closed 3D lumenoid with lumen
volume and pressure and a membrane shell. The mechanical contract is the same at
every level: the epithelial basal geometry drives the membrane, and the membrane
returns reaction forces to the basal degrees of freedom. An effective constitutive
membrane and an explicit collagen membrane are interchangeable alternatives, never
summed.

**How the work is staged.** The reproduction core is settled first — retire the
superseded membrane claims, freeze the faithful reference settings, and establish
reproducible stress tests. Then comes the direct numerical reproduction of the
paper's tissue and collagen-network figures, then verified 2D and 3D epithelial
studies that establish the cell-height and area response, then bidirectional
coupling with convergence and agreement between the explicit and reduced-order
membranes, and finally the actomyosin cortex, the closed lumenoid, and the new
predictive perturbations. The original collagen-network studies are that
reproduction core; one is kept as a central-force counterfactual, and the native
junction angles of another fold into the faithful reference rather than counting
as a new ingredient. The earlier idea that the network is soft because junction
angles are absent is retired by the cross-check against the released code.

**Engine note.** The downstream epithelial vertex model is `vivarium-tyssue`,
imported into the workspace as an optional dev sibling engine (R4–R6, E3–E4 build
on it). The collagen/actin LAMMPS processes run on `viva-lammps`.

**Driving schema.** The campaign is framed by the Barrientos et al. three-model
chain — collagen IV turnover (timer) → BM relaxation (network) → cell shape
(tissue mechanics) — reproduced as `viz/driving_schema.html` and mapped to our
studies: R6 realizes the timer/turnover model, R2/R3 the collagen network, and
R1/R4/R5 the tissue mechanics.

at_a_glance.role: Stage 1 membrane build. The staged protocol runs on real LAMMPS and the NC1-angle-stabilized network reports a finite elastic modulus (E ≈ 4.98 ± 2.15 LJ, ≈11 ± 5 Pa, 3 seeds; energy-scale caveat). Scoped honestly as NC1-angle-stabilized, not a full reproduction — only the NC1 junction angle is implemented; the released 7S angles (155°/60°) and the 7S break cutoff are not. τ is unresolved at this bounded scale (dense-multiseed mini candidate). Diagnostics / modulus-ladder / movies demoted to supplement.

Stage 2 growth-rate sweep (bounded-preliminary). At MATCHED strain the apparent stress σ(ε̇) is flat/overlapping across rates while crosslink density falls with rate — so the apparent rate-resistance is confounded by rate-dependent assembly time, NOT clean rate-stiffening. The earlier single-seed "≈7→11 Pa stiffening" claim is RETRACTED. A density-matched dense-multiseed run (resolving τ(ε̇) for a Deborah number) is the open mini candidate.

Central-force negative control (engineered-diagnostic). With junction angles OFF, the athermal modulus vs measured connectivity z (1.17→1.61, never near 4) scatters about zero with CIs spanning 0 — not reproducibly positive, by design. This control shows central-force counting does NOT reproduce the released (angle-stabilized) network; the z=4 Maxwell line is an idealized 2D heuristic, not a threshold for this finite-thickness network.

The faithful-angles headline. Forming NC1 junction angles DURING assembly gives a positive, reproducible modulus (per-seed ≈36.7/27.6/37.5 kT/σ³, ≈61–83 Pa) — in contrast to the central-force control (≈0) and the ill-conditioned post-hoc restraint (sign-flipping). So bending-during-assembly is what stabilizes the released model's mechanics; connectivity remains a covariate. (Only the NC1 angle is implemented; 7S angles are the stated gap. Reduced LJ modulus; Pa depends on the energy scale.)

Geometric readouts, two story-driven figures. Pore size (CDF + median vs areal coverage: 88→62→54 nm) reaches the corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at the densest condition — shown as a CROSS-SYSTEM reference, not validation for lumenoids. The NC1/7S-only topology under-bundles (mean 1.38 protomers/strand, 76% singletons, below the measured 5–7) because the released model has no explicit lateral-association bond — stated as a known shortfall. Evidence-map demoted.

Reimplements the paper's homogeneous tissue model — a fixed-volume cell against a viscoelastic membrane — and recovers the four confinement regimes by varying membrane stiffness and its relaxation time. The simple reference the spatial models are compared against.

Drives the collagen network through the loading protocol at several turnover rates, fitting the stress-relaxation time τ independently of residence time. On a dense multi-seed network τ is resolved across the full range and rises with collagen residence time — the Figure-2E DIRECTION (a floor-plus-residence relationship, reduced units), with a turnover-independent modulus. Observed.

Compares no remodelling, remodelling without new collagen, and remodelling with material insertion from one starting state. Only combined turnover + supply grows a connected load-bearing network (crosslink-per-area and rod-count ordering with-insertion > without > none, 3/3 seeds) — the Figure-2B/C ordering.

2D coupled growth (the meeting's #1 upgrade). A ramped PREFERRED basal area (division OFF) drives a REALIZED area that emerges and lags the target under a viscoelastic BM — a stiff/slow BM lags by a 0.317 gap (vs 0.116 free) and raises reconstructed height (0.70→0.91); zero growth gives no BM strain; a BM-stiffness gradient makes a spatial height gradient (0.76→0.91). Reduced-order 2D cross-section with fixed-volume height; qualitatively consistent with the paper's confinement direction, not calibrated. The resolved vertex-model sheet stays a static substrate at the engine level (named limitation).

3D monolayer growth (the geometric upgrade after R4). Preferred cell volume + basal area are ramped (division OFF) on the real 206-cell Tyssue monolayer; a stiff/slow BM reaction confines basal spreading (1.11 vs 1.20 free) while the realized volume lags the target (gap 0.27), and under the near-incompressible volume elasticity confinement drives volume into cell height (1.138 vs 1.133 free — directional). The full no-BM/elastic-BM/relaxing-BM control matrix + a relaxation sweep remain the calibration gap.

Carries an inferred collagen lifetime for control, perlecan gain/loss and growth-rate conditions through BM relaxation to cell shape, keeping inferred and predicted quantities separate. Reproduces Fig 7 — perlecan knockdown taller > control > overexpression shorter — after a review-caught correction of an inverted perlecan direction (overexpression shortens the collagen lifetime, per the paper). The growth-rate axis (faster growth → flatter) is also correct.

Extension, engineering verification (not in the paper). A coarse LJ bead cortex shows effective tension rising monotonically with the attraction (well-depth) PROXY — relabelled honestly as a proxy, not biological myosin activity, with seed/size sensitivity. Gap: no explicit filaments/motors, and the LAMMPS model exposes no strain input, so force-strain curves are not producible yet.

Extension, coupling unit-test. Occupancy-gated force transfer (traction = occupancy × tension; BM strain-rate = gain × traction) holds BY CONSTRUCTION — shown with a real zero-linker control (occupancy/traction → 0) and a bounded cortex→adhesion→BM smoke. Gap: force-conserving multiscale coupling and integrin mechanics are not established; it is a deterministic mapping, not emergent.

Extension, geometry verification. A closed 78-cell Tyssue shell with a labelled basal BM-coupling surface and a single enclosed lumen (section cut + scale). Gap: no lumen-filling drive is wired (pressure 0 at rest), so lumen growth and BM-regulated morphogenesis are shown as flat/honest, untested.

Growth-driven two-way feedback (the meeting's most-important follow-up). An epithelial PREFERRED growth trajectory is now wired (preferred cell volume + basal area ramped; division OFF), so basal displacement is growth-driven: the realized basal-area fold emerges and differs by coupling mode (two-way 1.006 vs one-way/uncoupled 0.767) while lagging the preferred target (1.150) — verified NOT hard-coded — and two-way returns a nonzero basal reaction tension absent in the controls. Reduced BM is the primary path; the explicit-LAMMPS BM stays a separate, numerically-delicate verification gate. Reduced units; magnitudes uncalibrated.

glossary.definition: One collagen IV triple-helical molecule (~376 nm end-to-end); modelled as one two-bead rod.
The two crosslinking ends of a protomer. NC1 binds one partner, 7S binds three.
The viscous stress-relaxation time set by crosslink make/break kinetics; calibrated to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime.
Equibiaxial in-plane strain rate. A sphere of radius R growing at Ṙ stretches its shell at ε̇ = Ṙ/R.

question: How does collagen IV molecular turnover set basement-membrane (BM) stress relaxation, and how do BM mechanics, epithelial growth and actomyosin mechanics jointly determine epithelial cell height and lumenoid morphology? (The original v1 sub-question — the effective modulus E(ε̇) and remodelling time τ(ε̇) a growing boundary produces, the two numbers the AICS vertex model couples to — is the P0/P1 reproduction core this campaign now builds on.)
hypothesis: Molecular collagen IV turnover sets the BM's viscoelastic relaxation time, and that relaxation — relative to the epithelial doubling time — controls growth- dependent cell confinement (Barrientos et al., Cell 2026). Replacing homogeneous tissue mechanics with spatially-resolved 2D/3D Tyssue epithelia, bidirectional LAMMPS–Tyssue coupling and explicit actomyosin should connect these quantities through forces rather than imposed constitutive assumptions, and predict when growth rate, BM supply, contractility and curvature change cell height and lumenoid growth beyond the paper. --- Reproduction core (P0/P1): a standalone collagen IV network, coarse-grained at the fiber scale (one protomer = one two-bead rod, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume), reproduces the Meadowcroft/Barrientos regime — a very soft elastic modulus (≈0.03 Pa published) and a crosslink-turnover-limited relaxation time calibratable to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime — and its E(ε̇)/τ(ε̇) feed the vertex model (offline coupling first).

executive.what_is_this: A coarse-grained model of the collagen IV basement membrane, built in Vivarium from the AICS lumenoid specification, grown into a reproduction and extension of Barrientos et al. (Cell 2026). The reproduction studies target the paper's Figures 1 (tissue-mechanics regimes), 2 (collagen rheology + supply) and 7 (perlecan/growth perturbations); the extension studies add spatial 2D/3D Tyssue epithelia, bidirectional LAMMPS–Tyssue coupling, an actomyosin cortex and a closed lumenoid. All studies now RUN end-to-end against their real composites and carry recorded evidence — but each is scoped honestly by evidence status (observed / reproduced / engineered-diagnostic / hypothesis / contradicted, per docs/figure-conventions.md), not scored as paper reproduction on a smoke test or a geometry screenshot. The membrane-build (v1–v5) and the paper reproductions (R1 Fig 1 regime topology, R2 Fig 2E direction, R3 Fig 2B/C supply ordering, R6 Fig 7 perlecan ordering) are the strongest results; the spatial and extension studies are preliminary. R6 reproduces Fig 7 only after a review-caught fix: its perlecan direction had been inverted and was corrected against the paper. FOLLOWING the 2026-10-20 modeling review, the spatial/coupled studies were refocused on the agreed PREFERRED-vs-REALIZED two-way feedback: R4 (2D cross-section), R5 (3D monolayer) and E4 (coupling) now DRIVE a growing preferred geometry (division OFF) and MEASURE the emergent, lagging realized geometry + cell height under BM confinement — the realized geometry is verified not hard-coded to the target. These are demonstrated in reduced order / reduced units (qualitatively consistent with the paper's confinement direction), not calibrated reproductions; explicit-LAMMPS coupling remains a separate verification gate. See meeting_alignment_2026_10_20 for the full spine + staging.
executive.verdict: The membrane model is complete: it reproduces the published elastic modulus and separates a reproducible elastic modulus from a reproducible remodelling time, giving both as functions of growth rate for an epithelial model to use. Two choices remain open, and neither is a flaw in the model — how to fix the absolute pascal scale (an energy-scale convention left to the authors), and the exact equilibrium crosslink fraction that the authors' monomer exchange and distance-gated breaking settle at. --- The build was checked against the authors' published code and its parameters corrected to match. The structure and central-force parameters agree (two-bead rods, one NC1 and three 7S crosslinks per protomer, no excluded volume, kT = 1, dt = 0.01, break-to-make ratio 0.66, formation probability 0.12, rod stiffness 200), and the authors additionally stabilize junctions with bending — an NC1 angle of stiffness 4.0 at 180°, plus 7S angles at 155° and 60°. --- With the corrected parameters the network is very soft: its elastic modulus is small and consistent with zero at this size (about ±1 Pa across seeds), in line with the paper's own ≈0.03 Pa. The remodelling mechanism is correct, but the relaxation time is below what this network size can resolve. --- The earlier idea that the network is soft because it is a central-force network below the rigidity threshold no longer holds: the published model has junction angles, so connectivity alone does not explain its mechanics. Creating those angles as the crosslinks form removes the ill-conditioning — the modulus becomes positive, reproducible across seeds, and well-behaved. With the angles active the network is not floppy; its modulus is finite and depends strongly on density. --- With the angle-stabilized network and the authors' dense starting geometry (3.0 rods per σ², a 12σ-thick slab), the model cleanly separates a reproducible elastic modulus (about 3 in reduced units, ≈6 Pa) from a reproducible remodelling time (about 40–60 in reduced time units); forming-and-breaking and forming-only crosslinking agree at about 2.6 crosslinks per rod, so the value is well defined where both were previously noise-limited. As the crosslink fraction rises, the modulus climbs through the published ≈0.03 Pa near the percolation point (around 0.8 crosslinks per rod) and reaches about 8 Pa when saturated — so the published softness is a sparse-crosslink state, not a gap in the model, and the apparent large discrepancy with the paper disappears. --- Reproduction campaign (R1–R6). R1 reimplements the paper's reduced-order tissue model and recovers the four-regime confinement topology across the two dimensionless axes (BM stiffness; relaxation/doubling time). R2, on a dense multi-seed network, resolves the stress-relaxation time across the full turnover range and reproduces the Figure-2E DIRECTION — τ rises with collagen residence time (≈37→102 reduced units over residence 12.5→200), with a turnover-independent modulus — scoped as a floor-plus-residence relationship, not a single proportional slope. R3 reproduces the Figure-2B/C supply ordering: only combined crosslink turnover AND material insertion grows a connected load-bearing network (with-insertion > without-insertion > no-remodeling, 3/3 seeds). These are the campaign's solid reproductions (direction/ordering, reduced units). --- R6 reproduces Figure 7 — after a review-caught correction. The figure review flagged that the model's perlecan ordering was inverted (it had perlecan stabilizing collagen → gain taller). An audit against the paper (Barrientos et al. Cell 2026: perlecan promotes collagen IV bond breakage, so overexpression SHORTENS the lifetime, measured ~1 h vs ~20 h control, knockdown ~500 h) fixed the perlecan_factor direction; the mechanics (relaxation → height) were already correct. R6 now reproduces the paper's ordering — perlecan knockdown taller > control > overexpression shorter — with a substantial effect (~19% loss-vs-gain). This is the figure review doing its job: a decisive sign error found and fixed against the source. The spatial (R4/R5) and extension (E1–E4) studies run and are preliminary engineering/verification results, not paper reproductions.
decisions_needed: Growth as preferred-vs-realized (2026-10-20): RESOLVED in direction — the first deliverable is now the two-way experiment where a PREFERRED geometry grows (division OFF) and the realized geometry emerges/lags under BM reaction (R4/R5/E4). Open: calibrate the stiffness/relaxation vs preferred-growth-timescale mapping and run the full BM control matrix.

Growth vs division (2026-10-20): RESOLVED for the MVP — growth is a preferred-geometry ramp with proliferation OFF; the paper's proliferation stays a separate faithful-reproduction extension. Confirm with the expert that no-division growth is the right MVP scope.

Explicit-LAMMPS coupling as a separate gate (2026-10-20): RESOLVED as policy — the explicit-BM path is a separate verification gate (numerically delicate, E4 F5), marked apart from the reduced-order primary results; stabilizing its subcycling is the open engineering item.

Perlecan direction (R6): RESOLVED — verified against the paper (perlecan promotes collagen IV bond breakage; overexpression ~1 h, control ~20 h, knockdown ~500 h lifetime) and the perlecan_factor mapping was inverted so R6 reproduces Fig 7. Left here as a sanity-check item for the expert to confirm the reading.

Lumen geometry vs model-side elasticity (2026-10-20): keep the new lumen geometry/volume (a geometry class computing enclosed volume) SEPARATE from model-side lumen elasticity/pressure; start E3/E4 from an already-closed lumen (no nucleation). Osmotic water-pumping is a later branch.
Reproduction conventions: the article alone does not fix every convention needed to reproduce it. Acquire the supplemental tissue-model equations and the precise Figure 1 parameter values.

Released turnover kinetics: pin down the grand-canonical monomer exchange, the distance-gated breaking, the 7S-specific mechanics, and the original stress-to-energy conversion before freezing the collagen reference.
Collagen supply law: a fixed concentration (for reproducing the paper) or a secretion flux (for the lumenoid hypothesis). Decide per study.
3D calibration data: obtain lumenoid geometry over time, cell height and volume, membrane thickness, and collagen-versus-laminin staining before calibrating the 3D models.
Actin fidelity: use a validated reduced cortical model unless a molecularly-resolved actin cortex changes a measurable prediction. An explicit go/no-go call.

Composite modularity: keep the collagen-network composites as thin selections over one general, parameterized network builder (chemistry, bending stiffness, density, and strain protocol as configuration), rather than near-duplicate generators.

Absolute modulus in pascals: the angle-stabilized model reproduces the published ≈0.03 Pa and gives a reproducible modulus in reduced units (E ≈ 3 LJ). An exact value in pascals additionally needs the released monomer exchange, the distance-gated 7S break (0.95), and the dense starting configuration — or accept the reduced-unit value and settle the energy-scale choice below.
Engine for the early stages: LAMMPS now, with Smoldyn revisited when surface binders are added.
Energy scale: report the modulus in pascals (fit to a measured modulus) or keep kT units and report a ratio.
Coupling contract: which vertex-model term receives the membrane — a basal tension, a mobility, or an elastic spring.
Linker values: density, spring constant, and off-rate; sweep the off-rate as a multiple of the crosslink break rate.
Growth rate: extract ε̇ from the lumenoid radius over time (still needed).
Slab thickness and layer count (one z-stack away).
Which readout calibrates and which validates: the remodelling time calibrates the formation probability and the time unit, so it cannot also validate.

studies.name: bm-v1-stage1-modulus-remodelling
studies.title: Elastic modulus & remodelling-time separation
studies.question: Can the clean-room collagen IV network separate an elastic modulus from a viscous remodelling time, as the paper's staged protocol does?

resolved_uncertainties: The viscous 'relaxation' densification was a fix-bond/break artifact — root-caused and fixed.
The ~0 modulus is rigidity-percolation physics (z < 4), not a measurement failure.
remaining_uncertainties: τ (remodelling time) — below detection until the network is rigid.
Absolute modulus in pascals — energy scale still open.

followup_study_proposals.title: Off-rate → τ calibration to the ≈20 h lifetime

findings.statement: LAMMPS `fix bond/break` models only over-stretch breaking, not a force- independent off-rate — small Rmax dissolves the network, large Rmax saturates it. Replacing it with a controlled random-deletion off-rate gives a make/break steady state and crosslink turnover.

evidence.observed: crosslinks 45→401 (old, densifies) vs steady ~54 then decay 46→3 (off-rate)

findings.explanation: Breaking must be length-independent to be a controllable rate.
findings.next_action: adopted in viva_lumenoid/collagen.py; guarded by a regression test

findings.statement: The v1 central-force network is below the 2D rigidity threshold (mean z ≤ 3 < 4), so its elastic modulus is statistically consistent with zero — matching the published ≈0.03 Pa.

evidence.observed: modulus −0.03 ± 0.06 LJ (95% CI, 6 seeds); mean z ≈ 1.2; z_max = 3

findings.explanation: Maxwell counting: NC1 beads reach z = 2, 7S beads z = 4, mean ≤ 3 < 4 → floppy regardless of crosslink density. (Scoped to the angle-off transcription; the released model carries junction angles and is soft for other reasons — bm-v3.)
findings.next_action: seed FP1 (junction-bending rigidity study)

findings.statement: The remodelling mechanism is now correct (stress decays as crosslinks break), but the relaxable stress is small in a floppy network, so τ is below detection at v1 scale.

evidence.observed: ensemble viscous decay ~0.29→0.25; s0 < 2·noise → τ unresolved

findings.next_action: resolve on a rigid (bending) network or a much larger ensemble

studies.claim: A coarse-grained collagen IV network (two-bead rods, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume) run through the spec's stage-1 protocol — stretch, hold, then switch the chemistry on — yields a separable elastic modulus and remodelling (stress-relaxation) time on real LAMMPS.

biological_validation.basis: Consistent with the published ≈0.03 Pa (near-floppy) modulus; the floppiness is mechanistically explained by connectivity (z < 4).

regression_compatibility.basis: No upstream regression baseline for this clean-room build.

Over 16 steps at 40 rods the round-trip is bounded (basal area 199.0 -> 160.1, lumen pressure 6.7 -> 78.1), and the feedback DIRECTIONALITY control holds: two-way basal_tension != 0 (e.g. +0.106), one-way basal_tension == 0 exactly. findings.statement: The explicit path does NOT inherit two reduced-path behaviors. (1) Subcycle convergence FAILS/inverts: bm_sigma over bm_substeps {1,2,4,8} = -11.4/-14.5/+28.6/+1828, the successive-refinement error GROWS (3.1 -> 43.1 -> 1799.6) -- more subcycling destabilizes the explicit BM rather than converging it. (2) The "uncoupled bm_sigma==0" inert control does not transfer: the explicit collagen patch carries intrinsic bond-virial stress (uncoupled bm_sigma +1.6 at 40 rods). The explicit loop is stable only at coarse subcycling (substeps 1-2) and a bounded network (~40 rods)/duration; 120 rods/24 steps diverges (bm_sigma ~4.5e4). A stable explicit-BM subcycling integrator + explicit-path gain calibration are the open items.

evidence.observed: explicit subcycle sweep DIVERGES (1799.6 >> 3.1); uncoupled bm_sigma +1.6 != 0; 120 rods blows up

findings.explanation: The explicit collagen BM is a stochastic LAMMPS relaxation with its own intrinsic stress and dynamics, not a smooth first-order ODE like the reduced BM, so re-running it more finely per coupling step amplifies rather than refines, and its undriven state is not stress-free.

studies.claim: The epithelium and its collagen basement membrane are coupled both ways: the growing basal surface stretches the membrane and the membrane's stress pushes back on the cells as a basal tension. On the reduced-order (effective) BM path the bidirectional loop runs end-to-end, the three coupling controls (two-way / one-way / uncoupled) behave exactly as the mechanism demands, and subcycling the BM relaxation converges. The EXPLICIT-LAMMPS-collagen-BM path now also runs the real bidirectional loop with correct feedback directionality (two-way feeds a non-zero basal tension back, one-way does not), closing E4's main gap. It reveals two honest departures from the effective-BM path: the explicit collagen carries intrinsic bond-virial stress (so the reduced "uncoupled bm_sigma==0" inert control does not transfer), and its subcycling DIVERGES rather than converges -- so the explicit loop is stable only in a bounded regime (~40 rods, coarse subcycling), and a stable explicit-BM subcycling integrator + gain calibration are the open items.

biological_validation.basis: Growth-driven path (NEW, the meeting's priority): a preferred growth trajectory is now wired (division OFF), so the two-way/one-way difference is observed UNDER growth; the realized basal-area fold emerges and lags the preferred target (two-way 1.006, one-way/uncoupled 0.767, target 1.150) and is verified NOT hard-coded. Reduced-order path: PASS -- the three coupling controls behave correctly and the BM subcycling converges. Explicit-LAMMPS-BM path: the real bidirectional loop runs with correct feedback DIRECTIONALITY (two-way basal_tension != 0, one-way == 0), BUT two reduced-path behaviors do not transfer -- the explicit collagen carries intrinsic stress (uncoupled bm_sigma != 0) and its subcycling DIVERGES (stable only at coarse subcycling / ~40 rods), so it stays a separate verification gate; stability + gain calibration are open. Reduced units; BM stress/tension magnitudes are not calibrated.

regression_compatibility.basis: The coupled_lumenoid composite is registered and the bidirectional coupling runs cleanly on BOTH the reduced-order BM and (now) the explicit LAMMPS collagen BM; the reduced-path behavior-test contracts in tests/test_p3_coupling_controls.py pass deterministically, and the explicit path runs bounded in its stable regime (40 rods).

explanatory_gain.basis: Establishes the epithelium<->BM coupling as a control-separable bidirectional contract and now puts the REAL explicit LAMMPS collagen BM in the loop -- and, importantly, shows the explicit path is numerically delicate in ways the reduced path hides (intrinsic BM stress; divergent subcycling), pinpointing a stable explicit-BM integrator + gain calibration as the concrete next step rather than assuming the reduced-path result carries over.

derived.insight: The bidirectional epithelium<->BM coupling runs end-to-end on the reduced-order BM and the three coupling controls separate exactly as the mechanism demands: two-way feeds the membrane reaction back as a non-zero basal tension (-0.2995), one-way feeds none back (0.0), and uncoupled leaves the membrane inert (bm_sigma 0.0).
